newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-KUMBLE RETURNS TO FORM AS W.INDIES STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KUMBLE RETURNS TO FORM AS W.INDIES STRUGGLE.

text.p: Indian leg-spinner Anil Kumble took five wickets as the West Indies struggled on the first day of the second test match at the Queen's Park Oval on Friday.

At the close of a rain-interrupted day, the West Indies had advanced to 239 for seven, an unbeaten 71 from Roland Holder getting them out of deep trouble after they had been reduced to 61 for three at the lunch interval.
Kumble also took five wickets in an innings in the first test and his performance signalled that he has returned to form after a disappointing tour to South Africa at the start of this year.

He claimed the wickets of openers Sherwin Campbell (8), and Stuart Williams (18) before later dispatching Carl Hooper (40), Junior Murray (11) and Curtly Ambrose (11) to the pavillion. Kumble finished with figures of five for 95.
Fellow leg-spinner Sunil Joshi, meanwhile, claimed the prized wicket of Brian Lara, who edged to a diving Mohammed Azharuddin at first slip while attempting to drive a ball from Joshi.
Lara never looked comfortable, facing 51 balls for his 14 runs in 65 minutes during the morning session.
The West Indies won the toss but only decided to bat five minutes before the start and may well have regretted the decision.
Holder, the only real bright spot for the home team, rescued the day with some crisp strokes and was involved in half century partnerships with Hooper and Ambrose.
At the close, Franklyn Rose was with Holder at the crease on thirteen.
